hub.meta_title: Letting agents in London | Hello New Home
hub.meta_description: London letting agents for every borough: 12% full management capped at £150 a month, no VAT, no lock-in. A London Local Partner and head office compliance.
hub.intro: Hello New Home covers the whole of Greater London, from the City and the West End to Bromley, Croydon, Harrow, Havering, Hillingdon and Kingston. Ina, our London Local Partner, does the viewings, inspections, move-ins and landlord meetings. Contracts, compliance, deposits and rent collection run from our head office in Swansea. Full management is 12% of rent, capped at £150 a month, no VAT, no lock-in. On London rents the cap matters more than anywhere else we work.

sections.h2: Who rents in London, and where
sections.html: London demand does not come from one place. The City and Canary Wharf bring professionals on long lets, and relocations that start as a furnished stay. More than 50 universities and colleges, UCL, King's, Imperial and Queen Mary among them, fill flats and shared houses from September. The hospital trusts, from Guy's and St Thomas' and King's to Barts, UCLH and Imperial, bring staff on rotation and contractors who want somewhere furnished for a month or a year. Further out, families rent in Bromley, Croydon, Harrow and Havering for the schools and the trains.

sections.h2: A Swansea head office and a London Local Partner
sections.html:
Ina Gutowska runs our London lettings and short-let management. She founded Divitiae Acquisitions, which sources property and supports landlords across London and the UK, and she shows your flat, meets you there, inspects it each quarter and does the move-in. She never holds your money. Her WhatsApp is 07775 801284.

Everything regulated runs from head office in Swansea: the tenancy agreement and written statement of terms, Right to Rent checks, deposit protection, rent collection, the repairs desk, the borough licence and the compliance calendar. We belong to a redress scheme and a client money protection scheme, both named on our fee sheet, and your agreement is with Hello New Home. The Local Partner programme explains how to open your own patch.

The ONS average private rent for London was £2,332 a month in August 2026, up 3.5% on the year, against £1,459 across England. At 12% an agent takes £280 a month from that rent; at 12% plus VAT it is £336, often with a 12-month tie-in.

We charge £150, because that is where the cap is, with nothing added for VAT. On the London average that is £130 a month and £1,560 a year you keep, or £186 a month and £2,232 a year against an agent adding VAT. The cap starts at £1,250, so it applies to almost every London property we take on, a Southwark flat at the borough average of £2,474 as much as a house in Havering. You can leave with 30 days' notice.

Licensing is decided borough by borough, and since 23 December 2024 a council can start a selective scheme of any size without government approval. This is the position in October 2026; we check every address before marketing.

  • Newham: selective licensing in 22 of 24 wards, 1 June 2023 to 31 May 2028.
  • Waltham Forest: selective licensing in 20 of 22 wards, 1 May 2025 to 30 April 2030.
  • Barking and Dagenham: selective licensing across most of the borough in three designated areas, 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2030.
  • Brent: selective licensing in every ward except Wembley Park, to 31 July 2028 and 31 March 2029, plus borough-wide additional licensing from 2 February 2026 to February 2031.
  • Croydon: selective licensing in 14 of 28 wards and borough-wide additional HMO licensing from 25 September 2026, for five years.
  • Tower Hamlets: borough-wide additional licensing to 31 March 2029; its selective scheme in Weavers, Whitechapel and Spitalfields and Banglatown ended on 30 September 2026 and no replacement had been designated when we checked in October 2026.
  • Southwark and Lewisham: borough-wide additional licensing in both, Southwark's to the end of February 2027, plus selective designations in Southwark to the end of February 2027 or 31 October 2028 depending on the ward, and in 18 Lewisham wards to 30 June 2029.

Letting without a required licence risks a civil penalty of up to £40,000 and a rent repayment order. The application is part of management. A house let by the room goes to hellomyroom, our shared-house team.

sections.h2: The Renters' Rights Act in London
sections.html: Since 1 May 2026 every tenancy in England is periodic and section 21 has gone. The parts London landlords ask about most are the ones aimed at a competitive market: a stated asking rent with no offers above it, no more than one month's rent in advance, and a reply within 28 days to any pet request, refused only on reasonable grounds. Rent rises go by Section 13 notice, once in 12 months, with two months' notice, and the tenant can challenge at the tribunal. A written statement of terms is required before the tenancy starts. The private rented sector database opens region by region from 15 December 2026; London's window opens on 15 July 2027, with registration due by 14 October 2027 (the regulations were still in draft when we checked in October 2026). We prepare your entry with you.

sections.h2: Long let, short let, and the next step
sections.html:
We run both, so we can tell you which yours should be. Short stays in London book through the year: hospital staff and contractors, people relocating for a job, students and visitors in every season. We price by season, and Flex Switch moves a property between short stays, furnished lets of a month or more and a tenancy with no re-onboarding. The free short-let appraisal shows both figures side by side, net of every cost.

Start with a free rent review: send the address and we call within one working day with a realistic rent for your street, the licensing position and a written comparison of £150 against your current fee. Ina will come to the property anywhere in Greater London.

faqs.q: Which parts of London do you cover?
faqs.a: All of Greater London, every borough from the City and the West End to Bromley, Croydon, Harrow, Havering, Hillingdon and Kingston: the E, EC, N, NW, SE, SW, W, WC, BR, CR, HA, IG, RM, SM and UB postcodes, plus the London districts of DA, EN, KT and TW. Send the postcode and we confirm straight away.

faqs.q: How much does full management cost in London?
faqs.a: 12% of rent, capped at £150 a month, with no VAT added. On the London average rent of £2,332 a 12% fee would be £280; ours is £150. Set-up is £295, waived when you switch an existing tenancy. There are no renewal, inspection or notice fees, and you can leave with 30 days' notice.

faqs.q: Does my London property need a licence?
faqs.a: It depends on the borough and often the ward. Newham, Waltham Forest, Barking and Dagenham, Brent, Croydon, Southwark and Lewisham all run selective or additional schemes, and others are reviewing theirs. We check the current designation for every address before marketing and complete the application as part of management.

Ina Gutowska, our London Local Partner, does viewings, quarterly inspections, move-ins and landlord meetings anywhere in Greater London. Head office in Swansea handles the agreement, Right to Rent checks, deposit, rent collection, repairs desk and licensing. The agreement is with Hello New Home and Ina never holds your money.

faqs.q: Can I short let my London flat?
faqs.a: Often, and because we run long lets too we can tell you whether you should. Short stays across London book year-round for hospital staff, contractors, relocations and visitors, priced by season. The free appraisal shows the tenancy and short-let figures side by side, net of every cost, and Flex Switch moves the flat between them.

sections.h2: The Renters' Rights Act in a London letting
sections.html:
Since 1 May 2026 every tenancy is periodic and section 21 has gone. The parts London landlords ask about most are the ones aimed at a competitive market: a stated asking rent with no offers above it, no more than one month's rent in advance, and a reply within 28 days to any pet request, refused only on reasonable grounds. The Act lets councils fine a breach up to £7,000, and up to £40,000 for an offence, which includes repeated or continuing breaches of the tenancy rules.

Rent rises go by Section 13 notice, once in 12 months, with two months' notice; a tenant can challenge at the tribunal, which can lower the rent but not raise it. A written statement of terms is required before the tenancy starts. The private rented sector database opens region by region from 15 December 2026; London's window opens on 15 July 2027, with registration due by 14 October 2027. We prepare everything the registration asks for and walk you through it; the entry is made in your name. If you need the flat back to live in or to sell, Grounds 1 and 1A need four months' notice and cannot take effect in the first 12 months of the tenancy.

Many London agents charge a percentage plus VAT with a 12-month agreement. When yours ends, or sooner if the agreement allows, we take the property over without the tenant moving: notice to the agent, transfer of the deposit and file, a check of the certificates and written statement against the Act and the borough's licensing map, and a visit from Ina so the tenant meets a face. Anything missing is reported before we start, and the £295 set-up fee is waived.

sections.h2: Next step: the free rent review
sections.html: Send the address through the free rent review. Within one working day you have a realistic rent for your street, the borough licence position for the flat, and a written comparison of £150 a month against your current fee, with and without the VAT your agent may be adding. Nothing is listed until the licence position is on file, and Ina can meet you at the property anywhere in Greater London.

faqs.q: Is the £150 cap really the whole management fee?
faqs.a: Yes. Full management is 12% of rent until that reaches £150, and never more, with no VAT added. There are no renewal, inspection or notice fees. Borough licence fees are council charges and are separate, and the rent guarantee add-on at £25 a month is optional.

faqs.q: Can you take over a flat that is still under a 12-month agreement?
faqs.a: When the agreement allows notice, yes. We serve it, transfer the deposit and file, check the paperwork against the Renters' Rights Act and the borough licensing map, and Ina meets the tenant. Tell us your end date and we work to it. The set-up fee is waived on a switch.

faqs.q: What is a bidding war ban?
faqs.a: Since 1 May 2026 landlords and agents in England must state a clear asking rent and cannot invite or accept offers above it. We market at the honest figure for the street and hold to it. Councils can fine each breach up to £7,000.

faqs.q: Who applies for the borough licence?
faqs.a: We do, as part of management. Head office checks the current designation for the address, prepares the application with the certificates the borough asks for and tracks the expiry. The borough's fee is paid to the borough.

faqs.q: How often will someone visit the property?
faqs.a: Ina inspects quarterly and sends a written report with photographs. She also does the move-in, the move-out and any visit a repair needs, anywhere in Greater London. Head office runs the repairs desk 24 hours a day.

shortlets.meta_title: Airbnb & short-let management London | Hello New Home
shortlets.meta_description: Short-let management across London: year-round hospital, contractor and relocation stays, priced by season. Co-Host 12%, Full SA 18%, free appraisal first.
shortlets.h1: Airbnb and short-let management in London
shortlets.intro: London has short-stay demand in every month, not just the summer: hospital staff and contractors, people relocating for a job, students between terms, and visitors in every season. We run short lets and long lets from the same team, price by season, and can move a property between short stays, furnished lets of a month or more and a tenancy with no re-onboarding. SA Co-Host is 12% of net booking revenue and Full SA Management is 18%.

sections.h2: Why London short stays earn all year
sections.html:
The guests are mostly working. The hospital trusts, from Guy's and St Thomas' and King's College Hospital south of the river to Barts Health, UCLH and Imperial north of it, bring locum, training and contractor stays of a week to a month, booked Sunday to Friday. People relocating to the City, Canary Wharf or a university post want a furnished flat for the first few months while the home is found. Students arrive in September and leave in June, and their families visit in between. Weekends and school holidays fill from visitors, and the big events lift demand in their own weeks.

We price by season and by day of the week: a higher rate for summer and busy weekends, a midweek rate for the hospitals and the contractors, minimum stays in the quiet weeks after Christmas, and a monthly review against what is actually booking in your part of London, never a city-wide average. A flat near the Royal London in Whitechapel and a house in Kingston book differently and are priced differently.

• SA Co-Host, 12% of net booking revenue: pricing by season, guest messages and the listing. You keep your own cleaner. The usual London starting point.
  • Full SA Management, 18% of net booking revenue, cleaning at cost: everything: guest vetting and messaging around the clock, cleaning and linen, restocking, repairs, reviews, the register admin when it opens, and one monthly owner statement with the night count for the business-rates test.
  • SA Launch, £495: photography, listings, a direct-booking page, pricing rules, house manual, the borough licensing check and the compliance pack. Waived with 12 months of Full SA Management.

No VAT, no 12-month minimum, and you can leave on 30 days' notice. Ina does the inspections and the owner meetings in person; head office runs the guest side around the clock.

sections.h2: Flex Switch: short stays, longer lets and a tenancy
sections.html:
One property, three shapes, one agent: short stays priced by season; furnished, bills-inclusive lets of a month or more for contractor, relocation, insurance and hospital stays, which suit the quieter months and mean fewer changeovers; and a tenancy, managed at 12% capped at £150 a month. Flex Switch moves the property between them with no re-onboarding and the same owner statement.

A let of a month or more to someone as their home will usually be an assured periodic tenancy under the Renters' Rights Act, and we say so before you sign. A national co-host cannot take a flat back as a tenancy and a high-street agent will not run it as a short let; we do both.

sections.h2: Business rates, council tax, the register and the honest answer
sections.html:
In England a self-catering property is rated as a business only if it was available to let for 140 nights and actually let for 70 in the past year. Below that it pays council tax, and several boroughs, including Brent, Croydon, Havering and Tower Hamlets, have charged a 100% premium on furnished second homes since 1 April 2025. We check yours, and the monthly statement carries the night count. The government has said a national short-let register for England will be running by March 2027; we register your property when it opens.

For many London flats the honest answer is the tenancy. A Southwark flat averages £2,474 a month as a long let, and a short let has to beat that after cleaning, platform fees and empty nights. We recommend whichever figure is higher, and we manage either.

sections.h2: Next step: the free short-let appraisal
sections.html: Request the free short-let appraisal with the address. You get the tenancy figure and the short-let figure side by side, each net of every cost and priced for your part of London by season, with the borough licensing position and the night-test position in writing. If the tenancy wins, the free rent review figure is the same one and we manage it at £150 a month.

faqs.q: Do short lets in London book outside the summer?
faqs.a: Yes. The hospitals and the contractors book Sunday to Friday all year, relocations come when the job starts rather than when the sun does, students and their visitors follow the terms, and weekends fill from visitors. January and February are quieter, and we set minimum stays and lower rates for them rather than pretend otherwise.

faqs.q: How do you set the nightly rate?
faqs.a: By season and by day of the week, reviewed every month against what is actually booking in your part of London. Summer and busy weekends carry a higher rate, midweek is priced for hospital and contractor stays, and longer bookings get a lower nightly rate because they mean fewer changeovers. We never price from a city-wide average.

faqs.q: How much does London short-let management cost?
faqs.a: SA Co-Host is 12% of net booking revenue for pricing, guest messages and the listing, with your own cleaner. Full SA Management is 18%, cleaning at cost, and covers everything. SA Launch is £495, waived with 12 months of Full SA Management. No VAT is added and you can leave on 30 days' notice.

faqs.q: Can I mix short stays with longer lets or a tenancy?
faqs.a: Yes. Flex Switch is included: the property can move between short stays, furnished lets of a month or more for contractors and relocations, and a tenancy, with the same agent, the same owner statement and no re-onboarding. We tell you before you sign which kind of agreement a longer let needs.

faqs.q: Is a short let worth it in London at all?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A well-placed flat near a hospital, a university or the City can beat a tenancy once midweek stays are counted; for many homes the tenancy wins after cleaning, platform fees and empty nights. The free appraisal shows both figures net of every cost, and we manage whichever is higher.

neighbourhoods.name: Central London and the City fringe
neighbourhoods.blurb: Flats in Clerkenwell, Shoreditch, Aldgate and Bloomsbury (EC1, E1, WC1) let to people working in the City, staff at UCL and Barts, and short-stay guests on hospital and contractor bookings. Rents here sit well above the £1,250 threshold, so the £150 cap saves the most.

neighbourhoods.name: North London
neighbourhoods.blurb: Converted flats and family houses from Camden and Islington (NW1, N1) out through Finchley, Wood Green and Enfield (N3, N22, EN1) to Wembley and Harlesden (HA9, NW10), with staff at the Royal Free and UCLH among the renters. Brent licenses every ward except Wembley Park, so we check the designation before any listing goes live.

neighbourhoods.name: East London and Docklands
neighbourhoods.blurb: Canary Wharf, Stratford, Hackney, Walthamstow, Ilford and Romford (E14, E15, E8, E17, IG1, RM1), with a tenant pool that runs from Docklands professionals to families along the Elizabeth line. Newham, Waltham Forest, Tower Hamlets and Barking and Dagenham all run licensing schemes, and we check every address before marketing.

neighbourhoods.name: South East London
neighbourhoods.blurb: Bermondsey, Peckham, Lewisham, Greenwich, Bromley and Bexleyheath (SE1, SE15, SE13, SE10, BR1, DA6): flats near London Bridge and the hospitals at Guy's, St Thomas' and King's, and family houses further out. Southwark and Lewisham run selective and additional licensing, and Elizabeth line trains from Woolwich since 24 May 2022 have widened the tenant pool.

neighbourhoods.name: South West London
neighbourhoods.blurb: Clapham, Balham, Wimbledon, Kingston, Sutton and Croydon (SW4, SW12, SW19, KT1, SM1, CR0): professional flat shares and family houses at rents that clear the cap almost everywhere. Croydon's selective and additional licensing schemes started on 25 September 2026, and we check each address against the 14 designated wards.

neighbourhoods.name: West London
neighbourhoods.blurb: Kensington, Hammersmith, Ealing, Harrow, Uxbridge and Hounslow (W8, W6, W5, HA1, UB8, TW3): flats for Imperial and Chelsea and Westminster Hospital staff, families near the Central and Elizabeth lines, and contractors around Heathrow who want furnished lets of a month or more. Short stays and tenancies both work here, and the free appraisal shows which pays for your address.
